title: Mathesis bank manifest, v2
description:
The shape of a record in bank/claims/ and bank/arguments/, and of the two files that say how records stand to each other: bank/relations.json and bank/topics.json. Derived from the manifests present when this was written, not from an intended design: a field is required here iff every one of them carries it. The two record shapes differ in an awkward way that is described rather than corrected — a claim is a flat object, an argument is wrapped in a single `argument` key — because changing either would rewrite accessions that are already published under a permanent serial.

RELATIONS AND TOPICS ARE ASSERTIONS. No kernel checks them. They are kept in their own files, attributed and dated, so that a reader can tell them apart from what a replay establishes — which is the whole reason this repository is worth reading. The one relation that IS derivable is deliberately absent: where an argument's graph contains another claim's root declaration under the same statement digest, that is a dependency, and `bin/mathesis` computes it. A stored copy would be a second and worse source for something already true.

accession.description: MTH.C for a claim, MTH.R for an argument. The public sequence is 6xxx; the 1xxx band is the internal corpus and must never appear here.

topicId.description: A slug, not the UUIDv5 used for `dictionary_id` and `profile_id`. Those are derived from a label that can change; a topic id is a permanent handle that a URL carries, and reads better in one. The inconsistency is deliberate.

doc.description: The statement's docstring. Absent on 2 of 32 — a record may carry no prose.

origin.description: `curated` is hand-entered in bank/curation.json; `deposited` arrived through the deposit system. Every record so far is curated. `deposited` is defined ahead of its first use, on the same reasoning as `source_url` being nullable: the distinction has to exist in the schema before the record that needs it, not be bolted on once one arrives.

pretty.description: The Lean statement as pretty-printed by the environment that built it. Rendered verbatim; never rewritten.

reference_sha256.description: The frozen reference export a discharging argument is checked against.

topic.description: Absent on 23 of 32: the corpus has been classified only as far as its first nine accessions. An unclassified record is not an error, and guessing a topic to fill the field would be worse than leaving it empty.

argumentFile.description: An argument file is the record plus its solution graph. The graph is what `nodes`/`edges`/`leaves` hold, and `argument.node_count` / `edge_count` are counts OF it — a mismatch there is a manifest disagreeing with itself.

axioms_reached.description: The axiom closure the adjudicator reached, VERBATIM from its report. bank/tools/verify-bank.sh requires exact set equality against a fresh replay — not subset-of-whitelist — so a manifest claiming fewer axioms than the proof uses fails.

export_sha256.description: Names the evidence: <sha>.export.gz on the bank-exports-v1 release. The blob is re-hashed after download, so this is the trust boundary, not the filename.

source_url.description: Null on every record so far. Typed as nullable rather than dropped: a record whose source is published should be able to say so.

node.description: A step in the argument. `doc` and `hypotheses` are present on some but not all.

leaf.description: Something the argument rests on rather than proves: a dictionary definition, or a cited result. `author` credits a cited leaf to whoever proved it.

relationsFile.description: bank/relations.json. How a curator says two claims stand to each other. `builds_on` is not a kind here and must not become one — see the note at the top of this file.

relation.description: An assertion about two claims, carrying who made it. `from` and `to` are claims, never arguments: the relation is between what was claimed, not between two particular proofs of it.

asserted_by.description: The profile making the assertion. A relation is somebody's reading of the mathematics rather than an output of the adjudicator, and it carries a name for exactly that reason.

kind.description: The three that no machine can settle. `generalises`: the source specialises to the target. `limits`: the source shows the target cannot be strengthened in some direction. `shares_definitions_with`: they are built on the same definitions and neither implies the other.

note.description: One line a reader can act on. Optional — the relation stands without it, and an empty note is worse than none.

topicsFile.description: bank/topics.json. Editorial groupings with no mechanical meaning at all: a topic is where a curator thinks a result belongs.

blurb.description: One sentence, for someone deciding whether to read on.

profilesFile.description: bank/profiles.json. One entry per depositing identity. Was one element for the whole bank, because one person curated it; a deposited record names its own author, so this grows. Exactly one entry may carry is_owner: the renderer picks the site's identity by that flag, and a second would hand it to whichever login sorts first.

id.description: UUIDv5 over the URL namespace of `mathesis:profile:{login}`. Derived from the login alone, so it is stable and anybody can recompute it.

citation_name.description: How this author is named when another record cites them, which is not always how they are named here.

avatar.description: A path under /avatars, when one was fetched. Null renders a glyph; a missing avatar is not a missing profile.

peopleFile.description: bank/people.json. The authors records CITE who have no profile here — they never deposited anything, and the bank names them because their work is used. No id: an identifier would imply an account that does not exist.

postsFile.description: bank/posts.json. The reading order, newest first. post_number is a position in that sequence and not an identifier: it renumbers when the sequence changes, which is why nothing else references it.

dictionaryFile.description: bank/dictionary.json. The environment a record was built in. ONE OBJECT OR A LIST OF THEM: the file holds a single object today, and the renderer learned to read either before the file changes, so the two repositories need not land in lockstep. A bank whose records come from more than one environment must use the list form — a record's dictionary_id has to resolve to the environment that actually built it, and a deposit is built somewhere the curated corpus was not.

id.description: UUIDv5 over the URL namespace of `mathesis:dictionary:{label}`, so the label fixes the id.

mathlib_rev.description: A 40-character git sha, or empty for a Lean-core environment. Empty is a fact, not a gap.

blueprint_url.description: Empty where the environment has no blueprint, which is every deposited one. A record's definitions link into ITS blueprint or into none — never another project's.

blueprint_labels.description: Declaration name to blueprint anchor, for this environment's blueprint.

$comment: anyOf rather than oneOf: an empty relations file and an empty topics file are both `[]` and match two branches, which oneOf rejects. The object branches cannot both match — their required sets are disjoint and additionalProperties is false — so nothing is lost. bin/mathesis does not rely on this: it validates each file against the branch its directory names, because the top-level alternation only ever produces the wrong branch's complaint.
